item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-62bb83b506a8b43f","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"In October 2023, Sheikh Hasina received the first uranium fuel consignment and fuel-delivery certificate for the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant. The project involved two 1,200 MW units, Russian financing and technology, planned Russian fuel supply for the first three years, and vendor take-back of spent fuel; officials reported substantial construction completion and planned operation from 2024–2025.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.3","1B.4","1B.10","5B.1","5B.6","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"2023; project implementation and future operation were reported, with safety and outcome claims partly prospective.","ruler_attribution":"The ceremony and project were presented as receiving Sheikh Hasina's support; implementation was by Bangladesh Atomic Energy Commission with Rosatom/Atomstroyexport.","limitations":["The source reports official and project statements and does not independently verify safety, affordability, or long-term outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6b02f012d077953e","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"At the October 2023 Rooppur ceremony, Sheikh Hasina said the plant design accounted for disaster resilience, affirmed an agreement for Russia to take back spent fuel, stated that Bangladesh would use nuclear power to protect peace, and expressed support for eliminating nuclear weapons and implementing the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons. She also identified the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Act, an independent regulatory authority, IAEA liaison, nuclear-fuel licensing, and a separately legislated operating company as safeguards and implementation institutions.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.2","1B.3","1B.4","1B.7","1B.8","1B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.4","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"2023; describes formal institutions, commitments, and implementation status at the time of fuel delivery.","ruler_attribution":"Sheikh Hasina made the commitments and attributed the regulatory and institutional measures to her government.","limitations":["The source does not independently assess enforcement quality, operational readiness, or compliance with the treaty commitment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d0b759c7706c3ebd","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"An IAEA Integrated Regulatory Review Service mission requested by Bangladesh in December 2022 found commitment to continuous nuclear and radiation-safety improvement, full cooperation, expert committees informing regulatory decisions, inspection activity, and an ethics code. It nevertheless recommended a national safety policy, revision of nuclear-safety rules, and a human-resources plan for sufficient qualified and certified staff; Bangladesh said it would incorporate the findings into an action plan.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.7","1B.8","1B.10","8B.4","8B.5","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The review occurred in December 2022 but bears directly on the safety framework operating during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The mission assessed the framework of the Government of Bangladesh and BAERA; the source does not attribute individual decisions directly to Hasina.","limitations":["The source is an institutional review and does not establish whether all recommended improvements were implemented during 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9d3bc7f920c212c1","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"A January 2023 CGS study reported that 74% of surveyed SME entrepreneurs experienced direct corruption after the Covid period, including bribery, political influence, extortion, nepotism, and unethical patronage. The report identified complicated licensing, lack of one-stop service, tax avoidance, customs-business syndication, and weak SME staffing/resources; an economist also said some government digitalization reduced corruption in some areas but procurement irregularities persisted.","question_ids":["5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","7B.9","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Study and reporting in January 2023, based partly on interviews from June–September 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The evidence concerns government administration and business institutions under Hasina's government but does not show her personal direction or benefit.","limitations":["The survey covers 194 SME entrepreneurs and is not a complete national measure; reported corruption is not individually attributed to Hasina."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e5e3a02816ce4df1","start_unit":1,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"In January 2023 parliamentary replies, Sheikh Hasina defended Awami League's continued rule, said elections were peaceful because Awami League was in power, blamed BNP campaigns and propaganda for questioning elections, rejected corruption allegations in megaprojects as baseless absent specified losses, and presented a Smart Bangladesh/2041 program involving infrastructure, investment, industrialization, agriculture, services, and higher income targets.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.6","4B.8","5B.1","5B.3","5B.7","5B.10","6B.1","6B.2","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"January 2023 statements and stated plans for 2023 onward.","ruler_attribution":"Direct statements and policy claims by Sheikh Hasina in Parliament.","limitations":["The source records her assertions and plans rather than independent verification of electoral competitiveness, corruption claims, or achieved targets."]},{"source_id":"SRC-99ca71bfd6036cb6","start_unit":1,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"In a televised election address delivered in early January 2024 about the 2023 governing period, Sheikh Hasina acknowledged possible mistakes and requested another mandate to correct them. She claimed an independent, financially autonomous Election Commission and reported major improvements since 2009 in poverty, water, sanitation, mortality, electricity, literacy, infrastructure, and economic indicators, while seeking continuation of Awami League rule through the January 2024 election.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.8","5B.6","5B.7","5B.10","6B.2","6B.5","6B.10","8B.1","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The address was published in January 2024 and summarizes the period ending in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Direct campaign statements by Sheikh Hasina.","limitations":["Reported achievements are self-presented campaign claims; the source does not independently validate the indicators or the Election Commission's independence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-46d295ca16047b8e","start_unit":12,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"RSF reported before the January 2024 election that journalists faced murders, imprisonment, violence, and attacks with impunity during 2023; it attributed censorship, propaganda, and tolerance of attacks to Hasina's government, noted arrest and legal action against opposition activists, and reported adoption of a 2023 cybersecurity law enabling prosecution of online government critics. RSF also reported army deployment for the election and a BNP boycott.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.3","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","3B.9","4B.2","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","4B.10","7B.2","7B.7","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Primarily reports developments during 2023 and the immediate pre-election period.","ruler_attribution":"RSF directly evaluates the government led by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.","limitations":["RSF presents an advocacy organization’s assessment; individual responsibility for every reported attack is not established."]},{"source_id":"SRC-203014319b084c8e","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"In October 2023, more than 60 public-health experts and organizations sought greater transparency and independent scrutiny in the WHO South-East Asia regional-director selection after Bangladesh nominated Sheikh Hasina's daughter. Critics questioned the nominee's technical and global-health qualifications relative to the role, while the nominee cited nearly a decade of WHO advisory and expert-panel work.","question_ids":["7B.3","7B.5","7B.9","7B.10","8B.4"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"October 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The potential nepotism concern arises from Sheikh Hasina's daughter's nomination by Bangladesh; the source does not establish Hasina's personal intervention.","limitations":["The article reports allegations and qualifications debate, not a finding of improper conduct or a final adjudication of the selection."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1ec7f00786229f9f","start_unit":12,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"RSF reported in February 2023 that the government closed the opposition newspaper Dainik Dinkal after a Press Council decision, while RSF disputed the legal grounds and said the regulator's decision was influenced by the paper's BNP affiliation. It also reported a proposed closure of 191 websites and seven serious attacks in two months involving ruling-party representatives, police, and affiliates, including beatings, abduction, torture, threats, detention on allegedly fabricated charges, deleted reporting, and police refusal to register complaints; RSF said Bangladesh's press-freedom ranking fell from 121st in 2009 to 162nd.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","4B.9","4B.10","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"February 2023 report on events from December 2022 through early 2023.","ruler_attribution":"RSF attributes the newspaper closure and broader pattern to Sheikh Hasina's government and reports abuses by ruling-party and police actors.","limitations":["The source relies on RSF investigation and interviews; it does not establish Hasina's direct orders in each incident."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d7cee085b26f0fec","start_unit":6,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"In November 2023, The Guardian reported that almost 10,000 opposition leaders, supporters, and activists had been arrested in two weeks after protests, with overcrowded prisons and many facing numerous criminal charges. It described attacks by Awami League activists and police at the 28 October BNP rally, deaths including a journalist, internet blocking, allegations of false charges and politically controlled police and judiciary, and a pre-election crackdown as Hasina sought a fourth consecutive term; officials denied political motivation.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","3B.9","4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9","4B.10","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"November 2023, directly within the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The reported crackdown occurred under Hasina's government; some allegations are attributed to opposition leaders, analysts, and rights observers, while government officials denied political linkage.","limitations":["The article contains contested allegations and does not independently prove Hasina's personal authorization of each arrest, attack, or internet restriction."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ca390040222b7261","start_unit":1,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"In March 2023, Sheikh Hasina said she would not yield to foreign pressure, rejected pre-election dialogue with BNP, asserted that the Election Commission was financially and institutionally independent, and cited voter lists with photographs, transparent ballot boxes, and election technology as safeguards. She also described targeted food support during Ramadan, including subsidized or free rice, and outlined preparations for LDC graduation, investment, exports, economic zones, and Rohingya shelter and services.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.6","2B.7","4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.8","5B.1","5B.3","5B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"March 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Direct statements and policy descriptions by Sheikh Hasina.","limitations":["The source reports government claims; it does not independently verify electoral safeguards, exclusion of dialogue, food-program incidence, or Rohingya service quality."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-df2bebc41f5b8bea"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied documents are uneven: several are official or campaign accounts, while the RSF and Guardian reports contain contested allegations and limited direct evidence of Sheikh Hasina's personal orders.","No supplied document materially addresses conventional international conflict conduct, nuclear weapons possession or proliferation, personal asset records, or independent verification of many claimed economic and welfare outcomes."]}
